analysis.summary: Management reported a standalone revenue of ₹1,173.25 Lakhs and a consolidated revenue of ₹11,642.04 Lakhs for the financial year ended March 31, 2026. The company's standalone net profit increased to ₹3,753.55 Lakhs while consolidated net profit stood at ₹6,853.79 Lakhs. Management highlighted growth vectors including asset monetization of the Prabha DP2 accommodation barge and international expansion through subsidiaries like Beluga International FZCO. No dividend was recommended for the year due to planned capital expenditures. Dolphin Offshore Enterprises (India) Limited held its 46th Annual General Meeting and published its annual report for the financial year 2024-25, detailing financial results, corporate governance, and operational updates.

demand_outlook.claim: The medium-term outlook for the offshore services sector remains favorable, supported by sustained offshore investment, increasing demand for specialized marine assets and limited fleet additions.
demand_outlook.quote: The medium-term outlook for the offshore services sector remains favourable, supported by sustained offshore investment, increasing demand for specialised marine assets and limited fleet additions.

demand_outlook.claim: Platform Supply Vessels are currently in high demand due to increased activity on offshore oil and gas platforms.
demand_outlook.quote: Platform Supply Vessels (PSVs) are currently in high demand due to increased activity on offshore oil and gas platforms.

demand_outlook.claim: The market is expected to remain buoyant as ONGC proposes high value tenders in brown and green fields.
demand_outlook.quote: The market is expected to remain buoyant in the coming years as ONGC proposes to come out with many high value tenders in brown & green fields.

demand_outlook.claim: Platform Supply Vessels are in high demand following robust activities on offshore platforms.
demand_outlook.quote: PSV are in high demand following robust activities on offshore platforms.

capex_expansion.claim: Dolphin Offshore Enterprises is planning for acquiring new vessels depending on the proximity of contract.
capex_expansion.quote: In response to this market opportunity, Dolphin Offshore Enterprises (India) Limited is planning for acquiring new vessels depending on the proximity of contract.

capex_expansion.claim: Dolphin Offshore Enterprises is planning a capital investment of approximately ₹500 crore over the next 12 to 15 months to acquire two DSVs/PSVs and two Anchor Handling Tug Supply vessels.
capex_expansion.quote: In response to this market opportunity, Dolphin Offshore Enterprises (India) Limited is planning a capital investment of approximately ₹500 crore over the next 12 to 15 months to acquire two DSVs/PSVs & two Anchor Handling Tug Supply (AHTS) vessels.

orders_capacity.claim: The Prabha is a Dynamically Positioned Vessel accommodation work barge with a capacity of 275 people, deck space of 1,200 square meters, and a 330-ton crane.
orders_capacity.quote: Prabha is a Dynamically Positioned Vessel (DP2) accommodation Work Barge with a capacity of 275 People, Deck Space of 1200 sq. meter and 330-ton crane and the same is owned by Beluga International DMCC, UAE which is 100% subsidiary of DOEIL.

capital_allocation.claim: Strategic expansion will be financed through a combination of debt and equity, aligning with the company's growth ambitions and current market dynamics.
capital_allocation.quote: This strategic expansion will be financed through a combination of debt and equity, aligning with the company’s growth ambitions and current market dynamics.

risks_headwinds.claim: Political unrest and war in the Middle East resulted in closure of the Straits of Hormuz and disruptions in productions from oil and gas fields and refineries.
risks_headwinds.quote: political unrest and war in the Middle East resulting in closure of the Straits of Hormuz and disruptions in productions from oil and gas fields and refineries.

risks_headwinds.claim: Fluctuations in oil prices can lead to reduced demand for vessels and affect profitability.
risks_headwinds.quote: Volatility in Oil Prices: Offshore vessels heavily rely on the oil and gas industry. Fluctuations in oil prices can lead to reduced demand for vessels, affecting profitability.

risks_headwinds.claim: Global economic slowdowns can lead to reduced investment in offshore projects and lower utilization rates for offshore vessels.
risks_headwinds.quote: Economic Downturns: Global economic slowdowns can lead to reduced investment in offshore projects, leading to lower utilization rates for offshore vessels.

management_commitments.quote: The Company expects these industry fundamentals to provide opportunities for long-term growth while maintaining prudent risk management and capital allocation.

management_commitments.claim: Dolphin Offshore Enterprises is planning a capital investment of approximately ₹500 crore over the next 12 to 15 months to acquire two DSVs/PSVs and two Anchor Handling Tug Supply vessels.
